- **What worked:** Using git diff --cached --unified=0 to extract only added lines was efficient - no need to read full file contents. The SecretScanner from src/secrets.rs was perfectly reusable without modification.

- **Reusable pattern:** For future git-integrated features, the pattern of 'git diff --cached → parse hunk headers → extract added lines' is clean and testable via unit tests with mock diff output.

title: Implement bf critical-path — dependency DAG float computation
description: Plan §4B.5: Two-pass walk on dependency DAG using recursive CTEs. Forward pass computes earliest start (ES), backward pass computes latest start (LS). Float = LS - ES. Zero-float beads are on critical path. Populate critical_path_cache table (already in schema). Integrate with claim scoring: 1000.0 / (float + 1) bonus for zero-float beads. Recompute cache on dep add/remove. Create src/critical_path.rs. Update CLI cmd_critical_path from placeholder.
close_reason:
Implementation completed in commit ac82d69 (feat: complete critical path DAG float computation) with fix in 215921d (fix dependency direction and backward pass computation).

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** Two-pass algorithm using temp tables for forward/backward passes. Forward pass computes ES (earliest start) iteratively from roots, backward pass computes LS (latest start) from leaves. Float = LS - ES. Cache invalidation hooks in add_dependency/remove_dependency/create_issue/update_issue/close_issue.
- **What didn't:** Initial implementation had dependency direction reversed in backward pass - fixed by correcting successor/predecessor relationships.
- **Surprise:** SQLite recursive CTEs don't support aggregate functions (MAX/MIN) in the recursive part, requiring iterative temp table approach instead.
- **Reusable pattern:** For DAG traversal in SQLite, use temp tables with iterative loops instead of recursive CTEs when aggregates are needed. Invalidate cache by calling invalidate_cache() after any graph-changing operation.
